top.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
top.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. top.title: Patriots vs. Packers weather forecast for NFL Week 9
top.description: The New England Patriots’ game in Miami last Sunday was partially played in miserable weather. This week’s contest against the Green Bay Packers will see a return to better playing conditions. The Patriots will be hosting the Packers at Gillette Stadium for a battle of 5-3 teams, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. At that point in time, WBZ Boston projects temperatures of 56°F, which will drop to 52°F at the half and into the high 40s toward the end of the game — noticeably cooler than last week, but most importantly with minimal if any precipitation in the forecast. “The good news is the risk of rain looks to be decreasing, clouds breaking apart,” said meteorologist Sarah Wrobleski on Friday morning. “But temperatures will fall from the mid-50s into the upper 40s, and we’ll have a breezy wind, too.” That wind is projected to bring gusts of up to 24 mph, which could create challenging patterns inside the Patriots’ home arena. top.description: Oct 31, 2026; Louisville, Kentucky, USA; Louisville Cardinals quarterback Lincoln Kienholz (3) rushes the ball during the third quarter against Stanford Cardinal at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Chris Carter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It took until the second half, but Louisville started to get more aggressive with their linebackers. On this play, Stanquan Clark times up the snap before shooting the gap to make a play in the backfield. He’s just unlucky because the play goes to the other side, which leaves him grasping for air. Stanford uses motion again on this play with a full shift of their tight ends across the field. Louisville tracks the motion, but you will notice that no one picks up the running back coming out of the backfield. So, on this play, Stanford takes advantage of two different issues UofL had in coverage earlier in the game. They don’t identify their responsibility after the motion, and they don’t account for the running back out of the backfield on a short-yardage pass. This is a nice play design and call by Stanford, but it would be nice to be able to say that the play just beat Louisville as opposed to the defense not even giving itself a chance. Lincoln Kienholz had his weekly instalment of “Man, it’s nice to have a quarterback who can do this” in the second quarter with his arm, but he does it with his legs on this play. I especially love the spin move that wasn’t really needed. I wrote about Louisville needing to attack the edges of Stanford’s defense in the What To Watch For post last week, so I was really happy to see them try to get outside a lot in this game. The first drive of the game was edge runs and swing passes, and they came back to it in the third quarter for this nice touchdown. As good as Isaac Brown is in space, he should buy dinner for Jaleel Skinner and TJ McWilliams for their blocking on this play. McWilliams is the outside receiver to the top of the screen. He gets up to the outside linebacker, who is flowing towards him before passing him off to Skinner, who gets outside after going in motion. McWilliams then moves up to the cornerback to create a tunnel for Isaac to run through. This is teach tape. I’m a bit of a broken record on this, but I don’t really understand why they can run this defense as often as they run Cover 3. Situations will dictate a lot of things, but the only real difference is that they are a little more spread out. Ben Perry would also not be in press coverage in the slot. He would be backed off a bit and could react to a run play. top.description: Danks offers Bayern squad update and discusses potential changes for Mainz clash Still in charge in Vincent Kompany's absence, Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks gave an update on his squad ahead of Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Mainz during a press conference on Friday. Danks revealed that Jamal Musiala and Aleksandar Pavlovic have both returned from injury to train with the team ahead of the game. “Most players trained yesterday. Jamal Musiala has re-joined the group, which is very positive. But tomorrow's game comes too soon for him. Aleks Pavlovic was also involved. We need to see how his legs react. Manuel Neuer trained again. Things look good there for the game,” Danks said. Asked about Musiala and Luis Diaz, who is also progressing in his recovery from injury, Danks said: "I think it's tough to set a date or game for their return. Next week they'll train individually and then be in full team training when everyone's back from the national teams. But there's no deadline." The Bayern assistant coach also revealed that some players could be rested, with Alphonso Davies among those who may need a break amid a congested schedule. “With a few players we need to look at workload and whether we rest them. Alphonso Davies, for example, needs a rest for his explosive nature. We'll make the decision today,” he said. “We’ll try out a few things. Perhaps Phonzy will be fine, just with restricted minutes. There’s a lot of rotation, a lot of movement, and the full-backs are involved in the attack. We’ve got plenty of players available there, which gives us options, as does our strong midfield. We’ll play as normal, in our usual style, finding solutions with different players. Who those players are, we’ll discuss that amongst the coaching staff. top.title: Coach who helped Sinner to the top set to depart
top.description: Sinner (left), with Cahill, has not played since winning Wimbledon in July [Getty Images] The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year. Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament. But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings. He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month. Swede Magnus Norman, the long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join Sinner's team for next season. "Darren has been an incredibly important part of my journey," Sinner said. "Together with Simone and the whole team, we have achieved things I dreamed of growing up. "He has helped me grow both as a player and as a person, and his guidance will stay with me throughout my career." Cahill had originally planned to leave at the end of 2025, but told Sinner at Wimbledon that the Italian could decide whether he stayed on - as long as he won the title. "Working with Jannik has been a special honour and privilege," Cahill said. nigeria.title: ANC gets 30% in South Africa’s election, partial results show
nigeria.description: South Africa’s once-dominant African National Congress was headed for its worst-ever election performance Friday with about a third of support after 80 percent of the votes from local government polls had been counted. Wednesday’s municipal elections were dominated by concerns over failing water and power supplies in one of Africa’s wealthiest nations which became a democracy in 1994 when the ANC took power. With final results expected by Sunday, the election authority dashboard showed the ANC was still the largest party with 31.8 percent of votes after 80 percent had been counted. Projections released Thursday by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), a state-funded research body, put its support at nearly 32 percent. This was its lowest score yet for the party after it secured just over 40 percent at the 2024 national polls and 46 percent at the previous municipal elections in 2021. At the heart of South Africa’s anti-apartheid struggle, the ANC — the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela — took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004. “This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared,” political analyst Daniel Silke told AFP. “It’s the ANC’s worst result in history.” “It will undermine its ability to exert authority across South Africa, not just at a local level, but frankly at a national level as well,” he told AFP. “And opposition parties will be smelling blood when it comes to the next election in 2029.” The party now led by President Cyril Ramaphosa has borne the brunt of criticism about years of municipal mismanagement that have left South Africans grappling with failing water supplies, persistent power cuts and crumbling public services. nigeria.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
nigeria.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027. The Bank has authorised capital of US$5 billion and is intended to finance projects across the energy value chain. Its establishment comes as traditional lenders reassess fossil fuel exposure, while African countries face urgent needs for electricity, clean cooking, infrastructure and industrial investment (APPO, 31 October 2026). The scale of the challenge is clear. The International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates that about 600 million people in Africa lack electricity and more than one billion lack access to clean cooking (IEA, 2025). It also estimates that meeting Africa’s energy and climate goals will require annual investment exceeding US$200 billion by 2030 (IEA, 2024). The central question is whether the AEB can help meet these needs while strengthening energy security, affordability and sustainability. Its success will depend not only on the capital it mobilises, but on the quality of its governance, investments and development outcomes. Beyond Financing Extraction The AEB can help address financing constraints facing African energy projects. But its lasting relevance should not be measured only by how much oil and gas production it finances. A bank focused narrowly on extraction would risk repeating a long-standing pattern: exporting raw resources while importing refined products, equipment, technology and manufactured goods. Africa’s challenge is to convert energy resources into reliable power, competitive industries, jobs, local expertise and improved living standards. Renewable generation should be considered alongside the transmission, storage and distribution systems needed to deliver power reliably and affordably. nigeria.title: US federal judge blocks Trump’s massive arch project
nigeria.description: A US federal judge blocked President Donald Trump’s massive triumphal arch project on Thursday, casting doubt over the future of the project hours after it was green-lit by a public commission. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, who is overseeing the case, ruled that the Trump administration cannot start construction on the arch for two weeks while the court considers challenges to its legality. The National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) had voted 8-4 to approve the project earlier Thursday, despite hearing hours of testimony from dozens of furious opponents who questioned its legality and purpose. Chief among the complaints was the location of the 250-foot (76-meter) tall structure: adjacent to the hallowed Arlington National Cemetery, the final resting place for hundreds of thousands of American service members. The giant arch would be much taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, its inspiration. It would also tower over the Lincoln Memorial, directly across the Potomac River. The four dissenting commissioners had called for the decision to be delayed, noting there were legal concerns, a lack of congressional appropriation to fund the project and questions about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s claims of the arch’s military use. But the majority on the panel, which is controlled by Trump allies, voted against a delay and the Trump administration said it aimed to start work right away. Chutkan’s ruling sided with several veterans and the attorneys general of Washington and Virginia, who had sued seeking to halt construction of the arch. – ‘Illegal project’ – The arch is one of several projects launched by Trump in a bid to put his personal stamp on the capital, many of which have prompted legal challenges. They include a White House ballroom, for which Trump had an entire wing of the presidential mansion demolished. The Supreme Court ultimately ruled that the plaintiff who filed suit to halt the project did not have standing. Another is the repeated renovation of the Reflecting Pool, a massive rectangular water basin on the National Mall. Trump has also proposed revamping the East Potomac Golf Links, a historic waterfront Washington golf course, cutting down hundreds of trees before a judge halted the project. The location, a traffic circle currently covered in grass, is key to the Trump administration’s defense of the project. Proponents claim that Congress approved the construction of a monument at the site over a century ago. nigeria.title: Trump bars future presidents from altering Oval Office
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump has signed an order designating the Oval Office as a national monument, a move he said would prevent future presidents from altering or demolishing the historic space. Trump signed the order on Thursday, extending his focus on White House renovations despite a major midterm election defeat suffered by his Republican Party. Critics have accused the president of paying more attention to construction and renovation projects in Washington than to voters’ concerns over the war in Iran and the rising cost of living, issues that featured prominently ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections. A day after Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump largely ignored the electoral outcome and instead showcased construction work on a new White House ballroom. On Thursday, his attention shifted to the Oval Office, which he has decorated with gold ornaments since returning to power last year, as well as the adjoining Cabinet Room. Trump said the proclamation was intended to protect the two rooms from future alterations. “It won’t be able to be taken down, destroyed, touched, or anything else. It’s called actually a national monument,” he told reporters. The president said the order would make it impossible for future occupants of the White House to carry out building work on the two rooms. The move, however, has fuelled speculation that Trump could be considering further changes to the West Wing, following earlier suggestions that he might relocate reporters from the White House briefing room, which is close to the Oval Office. Trump’s signing of the order was not broadcast by major US television networks. The White House has excluded CNN from the rotating pool of television outlets covering presidential events. The president, however, made a reference to the midterm elections, placing a red baseball cap bearing the word “veto” on the Resolute Desk in front of him. Trump, 80, has threatened to use his presidential powers to block Democratic-backed legislation, although he has also said he is willing to work with the opposition party. nigeria.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ set for blockbuster return after 13 years
nigeria.description: Fans of the violent “Grand Theft Auto” video game franchise are just two weeks away from getting their hands on the latest edition, which has taken almost a decade to make and has become the most expensive title in history. The franchise allows players to act out gangster fantasies — shooting up bars, crashing cars — in fictional renderings of US cities where the soundtrack piped through in-game radio is almost as important as the cutting-edge visuals. GTA VI, which comes 13 years after its predecessor, is expected to break sales records when it lands on November 19 thanks in part to a monumental marketing campaign that kicked off in late 2023 with the first official trailer. “It is going to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time,” Chris Dring of The Game Business outlet told AFP. During the 1990s and 2000s the game’s graphic depictions of sex, violence and misogyny became notorious — tabloid media outrage boosting the title’s notoriety and helping sales to skyrocket. nigeria.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. About The Founder OBIMI founder Helen Ewumi at the Nigeria outreach in Lagos. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. A critical part of thriving through a transition, a pivot or when you are starting over is to be honest about your limits. These could be the limits of your existing knowledge, expertise, and others. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. Founded by Carrie Crawford, ACL has presented African comedy live in the United States since 2019 and is built on a simple conviction: Africa’s comedy deserves a world stage, and a place to call home. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.description: U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth delivering remarks at the event hosted at the Consul General’s residence in Lagos. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. For 15 years, Omoyemi has built one of Africa’s premier fashion showcases, connecting Nigerian designers with American buyers and retailers and showing how trade creates opportunity for both our countries,” said U.S. Consul General Brandon Hudspeth . entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.description: Oct 31, 2026; Louisville, Kentucky, USA; Louisville Cardinals quarterback Lincoln Kienholz (3) rushes the ball during the third quarter against Stanford Cardinal at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Chris Carter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It took until the second half, but Louisville started to get more aggressive with their linebackers. On this play, Stanquan Clark times up the snap before shooting the gap to make a play in the backfield. He’s just unlucky because the play goes to the other side, which leaves him grasping for air. Stanford uses motion again on this play with a full shift of their tight ends across the field. Louisville tracks the motion, but you will notice that no one picks up the running back coming out of the backfield. So, on this play, Stanford takes advantage of two different issues UofL had in coverage earlier in the game. They don’t identify their responsibility after the motion, and they don’t account for the running back out of the backfield on a short-yardage pass. This is a nice play design and call by Stanford, but it would be nice to be able to say that the play just beat Louisville as opposed to the defense not even giving itself a chance. Lincoln Kienholz had his weekly instalment of “Man, it’s nice to have a quarterback who can do this” in the second quarter with his arm, but he does it with his legs on this play. I especially love the spin move that wasn’t really needed. I wrote about Louisville needing to attack the edges of Stanford’s defense in the What To Watch For post last week, so I was really happy to see them try to get outside a lot in this game. The first drive of the game was edge runs and swing passes, and they came back to it in the third quarter for this nice touchdown. As good as Isaac Brown is in space, he should buy dinner for Jaleel Skinner and TJ McWilliams for their blocking on this play. McWilliams is the outside receiver to the top of the screen. He gets up to the outside linebacker, who is flowing towards him before passing him off to Skinner, who gets outside after going in motion. McWilliams then moves up to the cornerback to create a tunnel for Isaac to run through. This is teach tape. I’m a bit of a broken record on this, but I don’t really understand why they can run this defense as often as they run Cover 3. Situations will dictate a lot of things, but the only real difference is that they are a little more spread out. But if this were first down, you would not be blitzing Kaleb Perry, who loops around on a stunt on this play. He would be right in the middle of the field to play the run. Ben Perry would also not be in press coverage in the slot. He would be backed off a bit and could react to a run play. If they were playing well in zone coverage, this wouldn’t be a problem, but at this point in the season I can’t understand why they haven’t adjusted. sports.description: Sinner (left), with Cahill, has not played since winning Wimbledon in July [Getty Images] The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year. Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament. But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings. He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month. Swede Magnus Norman, the long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join Sinner's team for next season. "Darren has been an incredibly important part of my journey," Sinner said. "Together with Simone and the whole team, we have achieved things I dreamed of growing up. "He has helped me grow both as a player and as a person, and his guidance will stay with me throughout my career." Cahill had originally planned to leave at the end of 2025, but told Sinner at Wimbledon that the Italian could decide whether he stayed on - as long as he won the title. "Working with Jannik has been a special honour and privilege," Cahill said. sports.title: How to watch U.S. Open Squash Championships, new Olympic sport
sports.description: The U.S. Open Squash Championships, a major international competition for a new Olympic sport, air Friday and Saturday on Peacock . The U.S. Open semifinals are Friday at 6 p.m. ET and the finals Saturday at 6 ET from Philadelphia. Squash was part of a group of sports added in October 2023 to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic program, along with baseball, softball, cricket, flag football and lacrosse sixes. Squash is a racket sport where two players compete in an enclosed court with four walls. Matches are best-of-five games. The first player to 11 points, with at least a two-point lead, wins each game. The Olympic debut of squash in 2028 will feature men's singles and women's singles events with 16-player fields. The tournaments will be held at the Comcast Squash Center inside Universal Studios. At the U.S. Open, both sets of semifinals feature the world's top three ranked players: Mostafa Asal (Egypt), Paul Coll (New Zealand) and Diego Elias (Peru) for the men and Amina Orfi (Egypt), Hania El Hammamy (Egypt) and Nour El Sherbini (Egypt) for the women. sports.title: Ex-PSG star Diallo to stand trial for alleged assault on team-mate
sports.description: Aminata Diallo (L) is accused of involvement in the attack on her ex-Paris Saint-Germain teammate Kheira Hamraoui (JAVIER SORIANO) Former Paris Saint-Germain women's star Aminata Diallo is to stand trial on charges relating to the assault on her ex-teammate in 2021, according to a court order issued Friday and seen by AFP. Diallo, 31, is believed by the investigating magistrate to have ordered the attack on her fellow former French international teammate and guided the attackers to where the assault took place. She is charged with complicity in violence and criminal conspiracy. Six others will go on trial alongside her. The date for the trial has yet to be announced. In November 2021, Hamraoui was attacked by two masked men, who hit her on her knees with iron bars, after returning from a team dinner in a car with Diallo. "After five long years of the case being investigated, it is a huge relief they have reached a conclusion and soon there will be a trial," Hamraoui's lawyers Julia Minkowski and Said Harir told AFP in a statement. "The whole truth will finally come out in this violent affair which is so rare in football, indeed sport, in which the victim was subjected to an unconscionable campaign of harassment following the assault." Diallo's defence team claimed there had been a lack of fairness in the investigation. "There has neither been a punishment nor questions posed about the methods used in the investigation regarding Aminata Diallo, which is also peppered with false statements," said Romain Ruiz, one of her four-lawyer defence team. "It's as if she has been crying in the desert for four years. We will call out her innocence till the final day of her trial." Hamraoui, 36, lost when she took PSG to a labour court last year claiming damages of 3.5 million-euro ($4m) alleging she was forced out of the club following the assault. Hamraoui was seeking damages from her former club, alleging a lack of support. She claimed she was "ostracised" on the pitch, in the changing room and suffered harassment on social media. sports.title: McIlroy fires 63 to move into Abu Dhabi contention
sports.description: Rory McIlroy is chasing a sixth successive Race to Dubai crown [Getty Images] Rory McIlroy put the setback of the two-shot penalty he received on Thursday behind him as he posted 11 birdies in shooting a nine-under-par second-round 63 at the Abu Dhabi Championship on Friday. McIlroy had been handed the sanction for improving his lie during the opening round and as a result finished day one on two under par, eight shots behind the leader, Italian Francesco Laporta. The six-time major winner was penalised after pressing down on the grass behind his ball with his club before hitting a chip on the par-four 12th at Yas Links. The Northern Ireland player responded in style in round two however to move to 11 under and assume the clubhouse lead with several of the leading players on the leaderboard still to complete their second 18 holes. McIlroy began his round with a bogey at the first but bounced back by picking up shots at the second, fourth and seventh holes. The back-to-back Masters champion then stormed up the leaderboard with five consecutive birdies from holes nine to 13. A dropped shot at the 14th proved to be only a temporary blip as he recorded two further birdies on the 17th and 18th holes to cap a scintillating round. It isthe first time in his career that he has made 11 birdies in a single round of a DP World Tour event. The 37-year-old is chasing a fifth Race to Dubai title in a row and a record-equalling eighth in total, that would draw him level with Scotland's Colin Montgomerie. McIlroy went into the Abu Dhabi tournament in third position in the standings, behind leader Eugenio Chacarra and second-placed Patrick Reed. American Reed was the long-time Race to Dubai leader after his Rolex Series victory in Dubai and win in Qatar but was recently overtaken as Spaniard Chacarra claimed a third triumph of the season at the DP World India Championship. Chacarra shot a second-round 71 on Friday to sit well down the field on three under, while Reed registered the same score to lie further back on one over. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai rankings are competing in Abu Dhabi, with the top 50 progressing to next week's season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

sports.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images The New York Knicks saw their fair share of celebrities between opening night and their NBA championship run, and two of the stars have lightly called out Taylor Swift. One thing that the New York Knicks winning the NBA championship did for the NBA is bring the celebrities out in full force. The Knicks have some of the most famous fans in the country. Names like Timothee Chalamet, Ben Stiller, and Mariska Hargitay were seen courtside throughout their entire run. Arguably one of the biggest musical stars in the world, Taylor Swift, also made a few appearances to root for the team during the run. She wasn’t at nearly every game like a lot of the other celebs, though, and it has led to her getting an unfortunate shoutout from Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride. Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride agree that Taylor Swift was the ‘fakest celebrity fan’ for the Knicks McBride was a regular for the Knicks off the bench during the playoff run. Kolek, less so, but he did play minutes in some games here and there. Regardless, both have a championship to their name now. And as bench players, they had some time to keep an eye out for the celebrities at times as well. The two spoke about ‘fake’ celebrity fans recently, and naming Swift ensured that the clip went viral. “Who’s the fakest celeb fan you’ve seen courtside?” was the question the two were answering on the NBA 2K show Deflected. “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek said, with McBride adding, “I would agree…Swifties not gonna like that answer.” Kolek then also said, “I’m gonna get some hate from the Swifties… I guess she’s got a lot going on so she can’t come all the time… but it’s a little performative.” Considering how passionate Swift’s fans are online, this is certainly a bold answer from the young Knicks duo. It might also be fair considering that the Knicks’ other celebrity fans are all extremely committed and vocal. It is a tough group for this question, and it seems Tay-Tay has drawn the short straw this time. technology.title: Bank of England pours cold water on AI productivity boom
technology.description: Despite the billions being thrown at artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered little in the way of productivity gains for UK businesses, according to the Bank of England. In its latest Monetary Policy Report , the central bank found that AI has increased UK productivity by an estimated 0.5 percent over the past three years. That works out to just 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points of additional annual productivity growth since early 2024, hardly the economic revolution Silicon Valley has been promising. "AI investment appears to be contributing somewhat to current demand strength, but so far there is only evidence of a modest AI-driven rise in UK productivity growth," the Bank said. Even industries supposedly best placed to benefit from the technology have little to boast about. Productivity growth has improved in AI-heavy sectors such as information and communications, but has yet to exceed pre-pandemic averages. That's not to say AI isn't doing anything for the British economy. The bank estimates that AI-related activity has accounted for just under a fifth of UK GDP growth since the beginning of 2026, though much of that appears to come from companies developing and deploying the technology rather than businesses becoming more productive by using it. "The contribution to growth from AI to date appears to reflect activity in the upstream development and implementation of AI technologies rather than broader gains from their adoption elsewhere in the economy," the report said. In other words, selling AI is proving rather more lucrative than actually using it, The bank also cautioned against giving AI too much credit for Britain's recent productivity improvements. Much of the increase appears to reflect businesses hiring fewer workers while output continues to grow, partly as companies unwind post-pandemic staffing decisions and respond to higher employment costs. And despite predictions that AI will make vast swathes of the workforce redundant, firms responding to the Bank's Decision Maker Panel survey reported virtually no overall impact on employment so far. The technology is, however, making some employers less inclined to hire new staff or replace those who leave. Other studies suggest businesses are still waiting for the payoff. A Gartner survey published last month found that while three-quarters of corporate board members expected AI to improve productivity and cut costs, just 3 percent of organizations had actually achieved their targets. Meanwhile, 38 percent were already over budget on AI spending, yet 85 percent planned to spend even more next year. Another study involving nearly 6,000 executives , published in February, found that more than 80 percent of firms had seen no discernible impact from AI on either employment or productivity. technology.title: UK ministers seek powers to investigate when AI agents are let off the leash
technology.description: The UK government is paving the way for rules requiring essential service operators and digital providers to guard against losing control of AI agents and report incidents when safeguards fail. An amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, which is passing through Parliament , would give ministers powers to regulate the deployment and reporting of agentic AI in certain organizations. The new clause was introduced during the bill's third reading in the House of Lords this week. In an explanatory note , ministers outlined plans for safeguards, notification of affected organizations, preservation of evidence, and government-led incident reviews. The measures would require consultation and parliamentary approval through secondary legislation. The move follows a series of incidents. Last month, OpenAI revealed that its agents repeatedly strayed beyond their intended scope , prompting the company to notify more than 100 organizations about the issues. That came after July's incident, in which an OpenAI agent accessed the internet and breached machine learning platform Hugging Face . The episode, and the potential for more damage from poorly designed AI agent deployments, have prompted MPs to question whether UK law can deal with such threats. Speaking to The Register , Stuart Davey, a partner at law firm Pinsent Masons, described the clause as "quite novel." Rather than directly imposing new duties, it would allow ministers to introduce rules and investigatory powers covering regulated organizations. Davey said that could include powers "to look where there has been such an AI agentic compromise or issue, and do some things... appoint inspectors, enter and search premises, seize and retain documents." Under the proposals, the minister could confer certain powers on regulators, requiring action from targeted organizations. Potentially affected organizations include gas and electricity suppliers, managed service providers, and cloud providers deploying AI agents for customers. Foundation model developers would not automatically fall within scope simply because they build the underlying technology. "Where there's a security or operational compromise in relation to a relevant network or information system, that would seem to capture those managed service providers or cloud computing providers who are using AI, and there's that loss of control," said Davey. He advised cloud and managed service providers to track whether the proposed measures become law. Evin McMullen, CEO and co-founder of AI identity and control infrastructure company AmanTrue, said the amendment recognizes loss of oversight or control as a security risk but does not itself impose new duties. "The amendment allows future regulations to introduce investigatory and enforcement powers where an incident involves an AI agent, targeting organizations running essential digital services," he said. technology.title: NHS wants a second opinion on Palantir's glowing self-assessments
technology.description: NHS England CEO Sir Jim Mackey plans to tell Palantir to clear future claims about its Federated Data Platform's benefits with his team – although he admits that could be difficult to enforce. Speaking to the Health and Social Care Committee this week, Labour MP Ben Coleman noted that NHS England had cautioned against attributing improvements directly to the platform, but said newly appointed Palantir UK senior vice president Tom Watson "is making claims that [Palantir] is making a difference, and that it's due to Palantir that changes are taking place." Responding, Mackey said he would write to Palantir and "tell them that they have to share with us and clear with us any benefits claimed in the future." But getting Palantir to comply could be another matter. "They should share them with us, but contractually, it looks hard to enforce," Mackey said. The planned letter follows repeated questions about the evidence NHS England and Palantir have used to promote the Federated Data Platform (FDP). NHS England awarded the £330 million contract to a Palantir-led consortium in November 2023 to help improve planning and efficiency. In July, campaign group Foxglove wrote to the UK health minister questioning figures used in Parliament to justify the contract. The Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR) also began examining the evidence. NHS England had said that as of June, 139 trusts used the platform, with 137 reporting benefits. It said an Inpatient Care Coordination Solution tool based on the FDP had helped hospitals perform procedures on an additional 111,589 patients. However, a Freedom of Information request later found that nearly a third of NHS trusts using Palantir's health data platform were performing fewer patient procedures than before it went live. Later that month, the OSR said NHS England had accepted that it needed to communicate its claims about FDP performance more clearly. The regulator noted that NHS England had published on its website a caveat saying that it could not "draw conclusions about cause and effect as other variables have not been controlled for." Last month, Watson, the former deputy leader of the Labour Party, sought to rebut what he described as misinformation about the FDP, repeating the statement that 137 trusts were already reporting benefits without mentioning the caveats. In a statement on X, Watson said the OSR had pointed out that there had not yet been a study on the FDP that controls for other factors like staffing level changes or industrial action. "That's a fair note of caution." In a prepared video, he said Northampton General Hospital, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton, and Chelsea and Westminster Hospital had all produced figures showing they are benefiting from using the platform. "Can we prove that every one of those procedures happened because of our software? No. But does that mean we should ignore what the hospitals are telling us? Of course not," he said. technology.title: Britain's tech ambitions depend on minerals made in China, MPs warn
technology.description: Britain's ambitions for AI, advanced chips, and clean energy rest on mineral supply chains dominated by China, and MPs say they cannot establish whether ministers have a credible plan to reduce that dependence. The House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee has set ministers ten tests for securing critical minerals. Its verdict is hardly glowing – it cannot be confident the government passes any of them. The tests cover whether ministers know which industries and technologies need protecting, what minerals they require, where supplies could be disrupted, and how domestic production, overseas partnerships, skills, and financing will close the gaps. In a report published today , the committee warns that diversifying supplies will take ten to 15 years, and will require sustained investment and cooperation with allies. Completely cutting China out is neither realistic nor desirable, it says. Leaving Beijing with so much leverage is another matter. Critical minerals underpin everything from batteries and semiconductors to datacenters and military equipment. The designation reflects their economic or security importance and vulnerability to supply disruption, rather than membership of an especially exclusive geological club. The UK – like pretty much all major industrialized economies including the US, the EU, Japan, and India – is almost entirely dependent on imports of these materials and mineral product s. But digging up more ore outside China would solve only part of the problem. The bigger bottleneck is processing. Citing International Energy Agency figures, the committee says China is the leading refiner for 19 of 20 strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent. A different flag over the mine does not necessarily mean a different route through the refinery. The exposure extends beyond chips and batteries. As The Register reported in August , erbium is used to amplify signals in fiber-optic links, while yttrium goes into components including ceramic capacitors. IEEE Spectrum warned that China effectively monopolized the processing of both into the industrially usable materials manufacturers need. That concentration has already caused disruption. China's rare earth export controls in April 2025 , introduced following US tariffs, rippled through manufacturing supply chains and forced temporary automotive plant closures. British manufacturers can suffer even when Britain isn't the intended target. The committee also highlights gallium and germanium, used in advanced semiconductors for radar, communications, and electronic warfare. China accounts for 95 percent and 93 percent of their global production respectively, according to the report [PDF]. Beijing flexing its leverage over chip materials is not new. technology.title: Safari's Autofill feature may be distorting time
technology.description: The autofill feature of Apple's Safari browser appears to be suffering from a date handling error that occasionally leads it to supply an incorrect credit card expiration date when filling out forms. The supposed issue has been a sore spot for Apple customers dating back at least to 2017, when the author of an Apple Community forum post complained about changes to the month field in the Autofill credit card expiration date when moving between time zones. "I've noticed for the last year or so, whenever I travel from Eastern time zone (my home) to Central time zone or even Pacific time zone that my credit card expiration date month changes in Safari Autofill," the Safari user wrote. Another post in 2021 raised similar concerns. "I don't know how to reproduce this," the author wrote. "Every few months Safari on any of my devices changes the expiration month of all of my stored credit cards by decreasing the month by 1, for example instead of 10/2029 it changes it to 09/2029." Three years later, another person posting to Apple's Community forum reported the same issue. "For a few years now every time I use Autofill on my computer my credit cards (ALL of them) always have their expiration dates change one month earlier," the 2024 post says. "I thought it was just a glitch on my computer but I bought a new computer and didn't transfer anything from my old one and it is still doing it." An unrelated Autofill bug report from 2024 suggests that if there is an issue, it resides in Apple-owned Safari code rather than Safari's open source WebKit engine. Wherever the bug may reside, Safari's unreliable handling of credit card dates has kept a complaint-filled Reddit thread going for four years. And the reported month-shifting has been noted in other threads, too. The Register was unable to reproduce the described behavior, but a reader insists it's still a problem. "The Safari AutoFill feature sometimes fills in the credit card expiration date wrong," the reader explained. "My credit card expires in December, but sometimes Apple helpfully enters November." "To be clear, the card is stored correctly when inspected in Settings," our tipster added. "The off-by-one error only happens when filling out a form in Safari, and not consistently." One possible way this might happen is if the Safari Autofill code implemented the expiration date using Swift's DateComponent type and stored it as a Calendar object with UTC as the TimeZone identifier. Doing so would anchor the date to a specific time. If the date components were extracted in Pacific Time, the value would be represented as eight hours ahead (PST). So 9/1/2027 at 00:00 would appear as 8/31/2027 at 16:00. Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but we're told Apple's Help Desk – or "Helpless Desk" as our source put it – advised clearing the browser cache and re-entering details of the affected credit card. technology.title: Hospital gave very sick doctor a special PC for his personal, erm, pleasure
technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to a fresh edition of On Call, The Register 's weekly tale of tech support trials and tribulations that readers kindly share. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Mason," who told us he once worked at a hospital doing tech support for its research labs. "One of the labs was for a doctor who was one of the world's top organ transplant researchers" Mason told On Call. The doctor was also a voracious consumer of – ahem – adult entertainment, a habit that saw his PC and other machines around the lab often come down with a nasty case of malware. Mason got to clean that up, sometimes multiple times in a single week. The doctor's foibles were widely known around the hospital, as was the fact that his activities violated several workplace policies. Mason pointed this out to his boss every time he cleaned up a fresh malware outbreak but such was the doctor's status that management never intervened. And then the hospital was hit by a nasty cyber-worm that did a lot of damage. During the cleanup, Mason's colleagues found logs that showed the doctor's PC was the source of the infection, and that he had been indulging in his online hobby at the time the worm arrived. Mason assumed this would be the moment at which the doctor would finally be held accountable and face disciplinary action. Instead the doctor made a bargain with the IT department to henceforth use only a designated PC when pursuing – ahem – personal and/or intimate matters. And he would only use office PCs for actual work. The hospital's tech team rescued a PC from its e-waste pile for this job. "Get this thing going and deliver it to Doctor Pervert," Mason's boss ordered. By this stage, Mason had had enough. He escalated his protests, telling his boss that indulging this doctor was unprofessional, likely exposed the hospital to lawsuits, wasted IT department resources, and was just wrong. "What do you want to hear?" his boss replied. "The CIO told me do this or get another job." After Mason prepped that PC, he only needed to clean up malware about once a year – after the poor machine was so overrun with malware that it no longer served the doctor's purposes. Mason left the hospital while this PC was still in place. "You'll be shocked, no doubt, to learn that years later the doctor's graduate students filed a lawsuit," he told On Call. "And that the separate fun-time computer was one of the pieces of evidence that the hospital knew about his – ahem – proclivities and not just ignored them but facilitated them." Have you been asked to cover up revolting behavior? Or ignore policy? Click here to share your story with On Call. It's our policy to tell a great tech support story week, so we appreciate every contribution. ®

technology.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
technology.description: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. Vendors of observability tools will be warming up their Indian sales teams today, because CERT-IN’s advice to Indian businesses includes improving their ability to log events, monitor for anomalies in real time, and send alerts. technology.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
technology.description: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations. One connection, works every time, needs no retries There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Feds warn grocers: Don't chill on cyber defenses as freezer hacking spree heats up
technology.description: If you have any industrial smart freezers, look out. The US federal government is urging owners and operators to disconnect them from the internet, apply patches, change default passwords, and take other security measures to prevent the kind of attacks that have become prevalent in Europe. “We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. Since mid-October, unknown miscreants have hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores in France, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden. The attacks increase the temperature inside fridges to highs of 50ºC (122°F), spoiling food, and sparking fires. The Register asked the FBI if it has documented any successful or attempted attacks against refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems in America. We had not received a response to our questions at the time of publication, nor are we aware of any documented digital attacks against these systems in American supermarkets. But there are signs that stateside operators are aware of the issue. Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, last month said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack that affected most of its US and European brands. Delhaize supermarkets in Europe are among those hit by the destructive freezer attacks. The Pentagon is also reportedly treating a series of freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the US in August as a suspected cyberattack, according to Reuters, which cited four officials familiar with the matter. In a Thursday advisory, the US FBI, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Health and Human Services, and departments of Agriculture and Transportation warned organizations about the ongoing cyber threats facing operators of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies said . Attackers exploit these flaws by bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and abusing weak configurations, according to the feds. Once criminals gain access to the systems, they can change the temperature to spoil food or temperature-controlled medications, start fires, and ultimately harm people who consume products that haven’t been stored at proper temperatures. How to stay frosty To prevent these scenarios, the government organizations urge owners and operators to “immediately” implement best practices and security protections. First and foremost on the list: do not expose industrial control systems and devices to the public internet. Ira
